title: Command Palette doesn't open with shortcut sometimes
author: RexLuscus56
summary: Command Palette activation fails only while PowerToys Settings has focus on 0.101.2362; later dedupe activity treats this as the canonical CmdPal focus-blocking issue for #50219.

status.label: Actionable design candidate
status.detail: The deterministic Settings-focus reproduction and later duplicate references justify a focused activation-path design investigation.

next_action.label: Queue focused design investigation
next_action.reason: Trace shortcut handling across Settings focus, CmdPalKeyboardService, and summon activation before exposing approve_design.

judgment.rationale: This is a credible current 0.101 issue because the failure is deterministic, scoped to a PowerToys-owned focused window, and later duplicate-digest activity keeps #50109 as the canonical issue for related CmdPal focus-blocking reports.
evidence: The reporter uses PowerToys 0.101.2362 on Windows 11 25H2, running as administrator.
CmdPal opens normally except when the PowerToys Settings window is focused; pressing Win+Alt+Z then produces the Windows stop sound.
The issue includes a PowerToys report ZIP, although automated triage could not parse it safely.
Dedupe digest #50263 marks #50109 as the canonical issue and #50219 as a duplicate-like related report.
CmdPalKeyboardService installs a low-level keyboard hook and MainWindow dispatches matched hotkeys through HandleSummon/Summon.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue a focused design investigation and keep stage design_in_progress; do not expose approve_design until the activation path and fix are verified.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette activation works generally but fails with a system stop sound whenever the PowerToys Settings window is the focused foreground window.
known_information: The report is against PowerToys 0.101.2362 on Windows 11 25H2, installed system-wide and running elevated.
The configured shortcut is Win+Alt+Z with no reported conflict.
The failure is limited to PowerToys Settings focus and is absent when another window has focus.
A diagnostic ZIP is attached, but automated triage rejected the archive structure and did not analyze its contents.
Dedupe digest #50263 later identifies #50109 as the canonical issue for #50219.
inferences: The Settings window may consume, reject, or alter the shortcut before the CmdPal summon path completes, but current evidence does not identify which handler produces the stop sound.
The issue is related to elevated-foreground focus failures but is narrower because the focused window is PowerToys Settings itself.
issue_context.analysis: The supplied reproduction is deterministic enough to start a code investigation without requesting another generic diagnostic. The linked duplicate digest strengthens #50109 as the right item to keep queued for design.
initial_investigation: src/modules/cmdpal/CmdPalKeyboardService/KeyboardListener.cpp installs a low-level keyboard hook and invokes the matching action id when modifier/key state matches.
src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI/MainWindow.xaml.cs starts KeyboardListener, wires HandleSummon, and sends HotkeySummonMessage through Summon.
Related #50219 concerns elevated foreground applications and was flagged as duplicate-like under #50109 by #50263; closed #45126 documents earlier elevated Task Manager focus behavior.
